author: gaxanh
content:
> calculate new_address as keccak256(0xff \|\| sender32 \|\| salt)[12:], where sender32 is the sender address left-padded to 32 bytes with zeros
I’m not overlooking the fact that the target address depends only on the sender rather than incorporating the initcode. That’s the minimum level of protection the protocol provides. I just wanted to keep it aligned with CREATE2 so we could inherit the existing design, but given the current semantic changes, that may no longer be particularly important.

That’s also fine, since TCREATE effectively gets both the capabilities of CREATE2 and a CREATE3-style ephemeral account.

author: gaxanh
content: One point that needs clarification is how SLOAD and SSTORE interact with TCREATE. The current motivation is to preserve compatibility with Solidity contracts, at least at the syntactic level. If that turns out to be pointless, I’d support disallowing them within TCREATE, which would preserve the stateless nature of the ephemeral account.
